Decide whether a sentence uses every letter of the English alphabet at least once, ignoring case.

Adapted from Exercism's [problem specification](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications/tree/main/exercises/pangram) (MIT). Listed under [Strings & Text](/examples/?subject=strings-and-text).

```nomi-run
// FILE: pangram.nomi
/// Whether `sentence` uses every letter of the English alphabet at least
/// once, ignoring case.
pub fn pangram?(sentence: String) -> Bool {
    letters =
        sentence
        |> String.fold_case()
        |> String.to_codepoints()
        |> Iter.to_set()

    Iter.all?('a'..='z', &Set.contains?(letters, &1))
}

// FILE: pangram_test.nomi
import pangram.pangram?

test "pangrams" {
    cases = [
        #("empty sentence", "", False),
        #("perfect lower case", "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz", True),
        #("only lower case", "the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog", True),
        #(
            "missing the letter 'x'",
            "a quick movement of the enemy will jeopardize five gunboats",
            False,
        ),
        #("missing the letter 'h'", "five boxing wizards jump quickly at it", False),
        #("with underscores", "the_quick_brown_fox_jumps_over_the_lazy_dog", True),
        #("with numbers", "the 1 quick brown fox jumps over the 2 lazy dogs", True),
        #(
            "missing letters replaced by numbers",
            "7h3 qu1ck brown fox jumps ov3r 7h3 lazy dog",
            False,
        ),
        #("mixed case and punctuation", "\"Five quacking Zephyrs jolt my wax bed.\"", True),
        #(
            "a-m and A-M are 26 different characters but not a pangram",
            "abcdefghijklm ABCDEFGHIJKLM",
            False,
        ),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, sentence, expected), description {
        assert pangram?(sentence) == expected
    }
}
```

## How it's written

- The sentence becomes a `Set<Codepoint>` and the check is
  `Iter.all?('a'..='z', ...)` over a codepoint range. Codepoint literals and
  ranges are what style §19 recommends for ASCII enumeration.
  `Set.subset?(Iter.to_set('a'..='z'), letters)` works as well; I picked
  `Iter.all?` because it reads as the problem statement. The predicate is
  `&Set.contains?(letters, &1)`, a capture.
- Case is ignored with `String.fold_case`, the function for comparing
  without case, rather than `String.to_lower`.
- The case "case insensitive" (uuid 2577bf54) is left out because canonical
  data replaces it with "a-m and A-M are 26 different characters but not a
  pangram" (uuid 7138e389), which is included.
